hints: Write z=x+iy, z*=x−iy, and remove the fraction using the conjugate of 2−i.
Equate real and imaginary parts, using zz*=x²+y², and eliminate x²+y² to solve for x and y.
Pair the coordinates into both Cartesian complex answers and check the original equation.
walkthrough:
Simplify the coefficient $\dfrac{5}{2 - \mathrm{i}}$ by multiplying numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate $2 + \mathrm{i}$:
$$\dfrac{5}{2 - \mathrm{i}} = \dfrac{5(2 + \mathrm{i})}{(2 - \mathrm{i})(2 + \mathrm{i})} = \dfrac{5(2 + \mathrm{i})}{4 - \mathrm{i}^2} = \dfrac{5(2 + \mathrm{i})}{4 - (-1)} = \dfrac{5(2 + \mathrm{i})}{5} = 2 + \mathrm{i}$$

Substitute $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $zz^* = (x + \mathrm{i}y)(x - \mathrm{i}y) = x^2 + y^2$ into the equation:
$$(2 + \mathrm{i})(x + \mathrm{i}y) - \left(x^2 + y^2\right) + 20 + 8\mathrm{i} = 0$$
$$(2x + 2\mathrm{i}y + \mathrm{i}x + \mathrm{i}^2 y) - \left(x^2 + y^2\right) + 20 + 8\mathrm{i} = 0$$
$$\left[2x - y - \left(x^2 + y^2\right) + 20\right] + \mathrm{i}(x + 2y + 8) = 0$$

Equate the imaginary part to zero to express $x$ linearly in terms of $y$:
$$x + 2y + 8 = 0 \implies x = -8 - 2y$$

Calculate the corresponding $x$-values using $x = -8 - 2y$:
$$\text{For } y = -5: \quad x = -8 - 2(-5) = -8 + 10 = 2 \implies z = 2 - 5\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{For } y = -\dfrac{12}{5}: \quad x = -8 - 2\left(-\dfrac{12}{5}\right) = -8 + \dfrac{24}{5} = \dfrac{-40 + 24}{5} = -\dfrac{16}{5} \implies z = -\dfrac{16}{5} - \dfrac{12}{5}\mathrm{i}$$
